title: Damped Oscillation: Why Real Springs Stop
topic: Damped harmonic oscillator — adding a velocity-proportional drag b·v turns Hooke's law into m·ẍ + b·ẋ + k·x = 0; the underdamped solution is x(t) = A·e^(-γt)·sin(ωt + φ) with γ = b/2m, and increasing γ takes the system from underdamped through critical to overdamped

beats.narration: Pull a real spring, let it go — it bobs, then stops. What slows it down?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Pull a real spring, release — what makes it stop?

beats.narration: Add air resistance — a drag force proportional to velocity. Newton's law gains a new term: m x double dot plus b x dot plus k x equals zero.

elements.content: Hatched wall on left, spring + mass displaced right, equilibrium dashed line
Restoring spring force arrow F = -kx pointing left from the mass
Velocity arrow v on the mass pointing right (mass moving away from equilibrium)
Drag force arrow F_drag = -bv pointing left (opposite to v)
−bv label above drag arrow
drag opposes motion, always
m ẍ + b ẋ + k x = 0

beats.narration: Divide by m, set gamma equal to b over two m, and the underdamped solution turns out to be a sine wave whose amplitude decays exponentially.

elements.content: ẍ + 2γ ẋ + ω₀² x = 0
γ = b / 2m   ω₀ = √(k/m)
elements.position: small mono caption below the equation

elements.content: underdamped (γ < ω₀) — solve the diff-eq
x(t) = A e^(-γt) sin(ωt + φ)
ω = √(ω₀² − γ²) — slightly slower than the undamped rhythm

beats.narration: Watch each swing fall a little short of the last, while the dashed envelope curves squeeze in toward zero — the amplitude shrinks, but the rhythm survives.

amplitude shrinks like e^(−γt) — but the rhythm survives

beats.narration: Crank the drag higher and the oscillation disappears. Crank it just right and the spring returns home in the shortest time without overshooting.

elements.content: Underdamped curve — bobs and decays (γ < ω₀)
label: underdamped (γ < ω₀)
Critically damped curve — returns home fastest, no overshoot (γ = ω₀)
label: critical (γ = ω₀)
Overdamped curve — creeps back slowly (γ > ω₀)
label: overdamped (γ > ω₀)
Damping never adds rhythm — it only steals amplitude.
